concept: Conservation of energy for the Earth
prompt: Explain how conservation of energy determines the Earth's mean surface temperature.
markscheme: In equilibrium the power absorbed from the Sun equals the power radiated by the Earth **(R1)**; if absorption exceeds emission, the temperature rises until the (strongly temperature-dependent) emitted power increases to match **(R1)**

prompt: A surface at 300 K has emissivity 0.90. Calculate the power radiated per unit area. $\sigma=5.67\times10^{-8}\ \text{W m}^{-2}\,\text{K}^{-4}$
Of the $340\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ of sunlight reaching the top of a planet's atmosphere, $102\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ is scattered back to space. What is the planet's albedo?

**(a)** State two factors that cause the Earth's albedo to vary. **[2]**

**(b)** Explain why melting polar ice can increase global warming. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Any two: cloud cover (changes daily); latitude/angle of incidence; surface type — ice and snow reflect strongly, oceans and forests weakly; season **(A2)**

**(b)** Ice is replaced by darker water or land with lower albedo, so more radiation is absorbed, causing further warming and melting (positive feedback) **(R1)**
The intensity of the Sun's radiation (power per unit area) at the mean Earth–Sun distance, measured perpendicular to the rays above the atmosphere, about $1.36\times10^{3}\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ **(A1)**

concept: Mean incoming intensity S/4 and equilibrium temperature
prompt:
The solar constant is $1360\ \text{W m}^{-2}$ and the Earth's albedo is 0.30. $\sigma=5.67\times10^{-8}\ \text{W m}^{-2}\,\text{K}^{-4}$

**(a)** Explain why the mean intensity received over the Earth's surface is $\dfrac S4$. **[1]**

**(b)** Calculate the equilibrium temperature of the Earth, treating it as a black body with no atmosphere. **[2]**

**(c)** The actual mean surface temperature is 288 K. Calculate the effective emissivity of the Earth–atmosphere system and suggest what this indicates. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** The Earth intercepts sunlight over its cross-section $\pi R^{2}$ but radiates from (and averages over) its whole surface $4\pi R^{2}$ **(R1)**

**(b)** $(1-0.30)\dfrac{1360}{4}=\sigma T^{4}$ **(M1)**, $T=255$ K **(A1)**

**(c)** $e=\dfrac{238}{\sigma(288)^{4}}=0.61$ **(A1)**; the atmosphere absorbs and re-radiates infrared back to the surface, so the surface must be warmer to lose the same net power — the greenhouse effect **(R1)**

concept: Main greenhouse gases and their origins
prompt: For carbon dioxide and methane, state one natural source and one source due to human activity.
markscheme:
CO₂: natural — respiration, volcanic activity, decay; human — burning fossil fuels, deforestation **(A1)**

CH₄: natural — wetlands, decay in anaerobic conditions; human — livestock, rice paddies, landfill, gas leaks **(A1)**

concept: Absorption of infrared by greenhouse gases
prompt: Explain, in terms of molecular energy levels, how greenhouse gases warm the Earth's surface.
markscheme:
Infrared photons emitted by the surface have energies matching the gaps between vibrational (and rotational) energy levels of the molecules, so they are absorbed **(R1)**

The excited molecules then de-excite and emit infrared photons in **all** directions **(R1)**

Some of this radiation returns to the surface, so the surface receives more energy than from the Sun alone **(R1)**

concept: Resonance model of the greenhouse effect
prompt: Describe the resonance model of infrared absorption by a carbon dioxide molecule.
markscheme: The bonds behave like springs with natural frequencies of vibration in the infrared range **(R1)**; infrared radiation of the same frequency drives the vibration at resonance, so energy is absorbed strongly at those frequencies **(R1)**

prompt: Distinguish between the greenhouse effect and the enhanced greenhouse effect.
markscheme:
Greenhouse effect: natural warming of the surface because atmospheric gases absorb and re-emit infrared; without it the Earth would be about 255 K **(A1)**

Enhanced greenhouse effect: the additional warming caused by increased concentrations of greenhouse gases from human activities **(A1)**
